question.prompt:
Let

\[ \begin{aligned} P(m) &= \frac{m}{2} + \frac{m^2}{4} \\ &\quad {}+ \frac{m^4}{8} + \frac{m^8}{8}. \end{aligned} \]

How many of the values of \(P(2022),\) \(P(2023),\) \(P(2024),\) and \(P(2025)\) are integers?

solutions.title: Check remainders modulo 8
solutions.explanation:
Clearing the denominators turns the question into divisibility by \(8\). Define
\[
Q(m)=8P(m)=4m+2m^2+m^4+m^8.
\]
Then \(P(m)\) is an integer exactly when \(Q(m)\) is divisible by \(8\).

Because \(Q\) has integer coefficients, inputs with the same remainder modulo \(8\) give outputs with the same remainder modulo \(8\). We can therefore check the eight representatives \(-3,-2,-1,0,1,2,3,4\).

For an even input \(m=2k\),
\[
Q(2k)=8k+8k^2+16k^4+256k^8,
\]
whose terms are all divisible by \(8\).

The odd representatives \(-3,-1,1,3\) have squares equal to \(1\) or \(9\), so
\[
m^2\equiv m^4\equiv m^8\equiv1\pmod8.
\]
Also, writing an odd input as \(m=2k+1\) gives \(4m=8k+4\equiv4\pmod8\). Thus
\[
Q(m)\equiv4+2+1+1=8\equiv0\pmod8.
\]
All eight residue classes work, so \(P(m)\) is an integer for every integer \(m\). All four requested values are integers. The answer is \(\boxed{4}\), choice \(\text{E}\).
